summary: William P. Chu worked in Buddhist studies, completing an MA at the University of California, Los Angeles by 2006. He also studied under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr. (attested 2006).

William Pettigrew (1869–1943) was active in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Ardington Aborigines Mission Training Centre (~1888–1890) and served as a missionary with the American Baptist Missionary Union starting in 1894.

William Price (1780–1830) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served on Gore Ouseley's Mission to Persia (1811–1812) and taught at Fort William College in 1813 and from 1824.

William R. Hutchison (1930–2005) worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Oxford (~1951–1953) and Yale (~1953–1956), later holding posts at Yale, Hunter College, Wisconsin-Madison, American University (~1960–1968), and Harvard (1968).

William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin, Michigan, and Chicago, he held faculty posts at Princeton (~1971–1978), UCLA (~1978–1989), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1989–2010).

William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) worked in linguistics and religious studies. Educated at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, he taught at Yale and served as president of Bradley University (~1897–1899) and the University of Chicago (1891–1906).

William Reeve (1794–1850) worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society (~1815–1824 and ~1827–1834) and later as minister at Oswestry Congregational Church (1836–1843).
William Robertson (1721–1793) was a historian who studied divinity at the University of Edinburgh from 1733 to 1741. He later served as the Principal of the University of Edinburgh from 1762 to 1792.

William Ross Hardie (1862–1916) studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1876–1880) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1880–1884). He held academic posts at the University of Oxford (~1884–1895) and the University of Edinburgh (~1895–1916).

William Roxburgh (1751–1815) was a botanist in Indology who studied at Edinburgh under John Hope and Alexander Monro, and at Aberdeen. He served as Chief Botanist for the East India Company and superintendent of the Calcutta Botanic Garden (1793–1813).

William S. Waldron specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, supervised by Minoru Kiyota, Ichijo Ogawa, and Seiki Miyashita, and later held positions at Otani University and Middlebury College.

William Sandys Wright Vaux (1818–1885) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology educated at Balliol College, Oxford. He served at the British Museum (1841–1870), presided over the Royal Numismatic Society (1855–1874), and was Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1876–1885).

William Sax (born 1957) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He held an academic post at the University of Canterbury (attested 2000) and became Professor Emeritus at Heidelberg University in 2025.

William Sidney Allen (1918–2004) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and Arthur James Beattie. He lectured at SOAS (1948–1951) and served as Professor of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1955–1982).

William Spottiswoode (1825–1883) was an Indologist who studied at Balliol College, Oxford (1842–1845). He held a post at Balliol College in 1846 and joined the firm Eyre & Spottiswoode that same year.

William Stede (1882–1958) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who earned his PhD at Leipzig. He taught at the University of Liverpool (1908–1911) and SOAS (1926–1949), and served as President of the Pali Text Society (1950–1958).
William Taylor (1800–1849) was active in Indology. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society from 1824 to 1845 and worked as a cataloguer at Madras College.

William Van Gordon works in Buddhist and religious studies. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University in 2015.

William W. Malandra (born 1942) is a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities as a Professor (~1972–2007) and later Professor Emeritus (~2007).

William Ward (1769–1823) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied under John Fawcett at Ewood Hall Academy (1797) and worked at the Serampore Mission (~1799–1823), where he co-founded Serampore College in 1818.
